messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert: GPU_OOM_ALERT fired for pool=gpu-pool-west2a. Count=8 failures in 3m. PagerDuty: https://pagerduty.example/PD12345 :rotating_light:

ben: Acked. I'm on it. Starting triage — will check node logs and recent deploys.

carla: I see repeated CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY on g-109 and g-112, plus cublas alloc failures. Dumping last 3 logs:

```
[2026-03-15T00:02:12Z] ERROR runtime: cuda: CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY at step=generate, alloc=78000000000
[2026-03-15T00:02:12Z] ERROR runtime: cublas: CUBLAS_STATUS_ALLOC_FAILED
[2026-03-15T00:02:13Z] WARN  runtime: nvmlDeviceGetMemoryInfo: free=0 used=80GB total=80GB
```

alice: Not a deploy — no rollouts in past 2 hours. Load spike on mid-night batch jobs? Checking traffic patterns.

dave: Support seeing elevated 5xx for customers: AcmeCorp (~120 rpm failing), BetaAI (~45 rpm). Tickets #7892 #7893. Timestamp ~00:02Z.

erica: CS flagged latency spikes for enterprise customers — they reported failures in their streaming endpoints.

ben: Quick mitigation: enable autoshedder to drop low-priority queued requests and reroute to fallback-model-quant2. Applying now.

carla: Applied routing override: set route(general-gpu)->fallback-model-quant2 (strict) and reduced batch_size from 16 to 1 for affected route. Commands:

```
$ infractl routes override --route general-gpu --to fallback-model-quant2 --force
$ infractl models update-config fallback-model-quant2 --batch-size 1
```

ben: Also scaling up warm pool by +2 A100-80GB (scaling group gpu-west2a-warm). Kicked off infra job.

alice: Infra logs show warm pool instances provisioning (g-201,g-202). ETA ~120s.

dave: After reroute some customers still see errors but most successful requests now use fallback-model-quant2. AcmeCorp errors down from 120->15 rpm.

carla: Observed further OOMs on g-109 during drain attempt — looks like a memory leak in kv-cache for long-context jobs. Initiating controlled evacuate of g-109.

ben: Marking nodes g-109,g-112 as drain and disabling scheduling to them.

```
$ infractl nodes drain g-109 g-112 --reason "OOM cascade"
```

alice: Drains started. Evac logs show some long requests timed out during requeue, ~8 requests dropped. Not ideal.

dave: Notifying impacted customers with ETA for full recovery ~10-15m. CS drafting message.

erica: Please include mitigation (fallback model, reduced batch) and suggestion to retry after 60s.

ben: PD: escalated to eng-runtime lead (@carla) and infra lead (@alice). PagerDuty note updated.

carla: Taking on-call lead. I'll keep this thread as source of truth. Plan: monitor for 30m, validate no new OOMs, run a small hotfix to kv-cache eviction to reduce retention.

alice: Hotfix prepared: change kv_cache_retention_ms 60000 -> 15000. Rolling to 10% first.

ben: Rollout started. Patch applied to 10% of runtime pods.

carla: No new OOMs in last 90s on warmed nodes. g-109 evacuation finishing. Warm pool healthy.

dave: Customers updated. Support closing high-priority tickets pending stabilization.

ben: Handoff if stable: I need sleep, passing to carla for next 30m watch. Summary: PD alert GPU_OOM_ALERT -> acked -> fallback model + batch reduction -> scale warm pool + drain faulty nodes -> kv_cache retention hotfix rolling -> visible customer impact reduced from ~120->15 rpm and trending down.

carla: Accepted. I'll ping when fully clear or if any regression. Filing postmortem template and action items: 1) root cause analysis kv-cache leak with long-context, 2) add better early-shed for long-lived requests, 3) extend warm pool buffer, 4) alert tuning to reduce noisy PD churn. Assigning owners after stabilization. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: PagerDuty: Alert resolved (auto) for GPU_OOM_ALERT at 00:20Z. PD-Runbook: https://pagerduty.example/runbooks/gpu-oom

carla: Closing thread for now, will update PM/ENG and schedule follow-up. Thanks all :heart:
